title: Cursor Automations - Event and Schedule Driven Cloud Agents
description:
In this workshop, we build Cursor Automations , cloud agents triggered by events or schedules to automate the software development lifecycle.

Topics covered:

Automations \& agent teammates:

Automations let you build a fleet of agent teammates running on cloud agents (Cursor-hosted or self-hosted VMs) to automate SDLC toil like bug triage, feature-flag cleanup, and reviews.

Anatomy of an automation:

Each automation has a repo (single or multi), a trigger like a Slack message, schedule, or PR, a system prompt, a model, and tools such as Jira and Slack.

Version control with skills:

Codify the core of each automation as a skill in your .cursor folder for version control. Run history, success and failure counts, and audit logs help you debug and tune them.

Productized automations:

Beyond custom ones, BugBot reviews PRs and can autofix by spinning up a cloud agent, while Security Review gives risk scores, configurable at the PR, repo, or org level.

Repo-less automations:

Automations can run without a codebase as general-purpose agents , daily industry briefs, after-hours Slack digests, or even image generation.

segments.heading: Core Concepts and Architectural Foundations of Cursor Automations - Event and Schedule Driven Cloud Agents
segments.text: In this session on Cursor Automations - Event and Schedule Driven Cloud Agents, the focus centers on understanding the practical design patterns and developer workflows enabled by modern AI-assisted engineering. As development teams adopt agentic systems, the boundaries between manual code authorship and automated synthesis begin to blur. The speakers emphasize that establishing reliable context is paramount: providing the right repository structure, explicit project rules, and scoped documentation allows the underlying models to generate precise, syntactically correct implementations. By anchoring the discussion in real-world scenarios, the talk demonstrates how engineering productivity accelerates when tools operate directly within the IDE, reducing friction and eliminating disruptive context switching across disjointed external interfaces.

segments.heading: Technical Implementation, Tooling, and Workflow Patterns
segments.text: Diving deeper into operational mechanics, the presentation details how specific platform capabilities interact to execute complex programming tasks. Key components such as Cursor, Cursor Automations, Bugbot work in concert to maintain project state and navigate intricate dependency graphs. The session highlights the importance of deterministic tool calling, background agent execution, and structured feedback loops. Developers are guided through concrete demonstrations showing how natural language prompts are parsed into multi-file diffs, verified against local unit tests, and iteratively refined before final commit. This pattern ensures high reliability across both legacy refactoring and greenfield service development.

segments.heading: Evaluation, Best Practices, and Future Directions
segments.text: The concluding segment addresses best practices for scaling agent-driven development across larger teams. Speakers discuss token efficiency, model selection economics, and safety guardrails required when granting agents access to internal APIs and production repositories. Teams must establish clear evaluation benchmarks to verify that automated contributions maintain rigorous security and code quality standards. By combining automated linting, continuous integration checks, and human-in-the-loop review, organizations can safely harness autonomous agents to resolve routine maintenance tasks, documentation updates, and cross-repository migrations while preserving engineering velocity.
